TO AND FROM MALAYSIA

under the provisions of any law in force in Malaysia, ajudicial has issued a warrant authorising the arrest of a person accused or convicted of an offence and that person is or is believed to be in Brunei a Magistrate in Brunei Darussalam may, if satisfied that the was duly issued in Malaysia, endorse the warrant, and the warrant may then be executed on that person as if it were a warrant lawfully issued in Brunei Darussalam under the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Code.

under the provisions of any law in force in Malaysia to rule 2, a warrant issued by a Magistrate or a Magistrate's in Brunei Darussalam has been endorsed by a Magistrate in and executed on the person named in the warrant, the warrant for the purposes of these Rules be deemed to have been as validly as if the execution had been effected in Brunei Darussalam.

a warrant has been executed in Brunei Darussalam pursuant of to rule 2, the person arrested shall be produced as soon as possible before to a Magistrate in Brunei Darussalam, who shall, if satisfied that he is the specified in the warrant, that the arrested person be or Singapore forthwith in custody to the appropriate court in Malaysia; and any such person shall, while in such custody, be deemed for all purposes to be in lawful custody: that such Magistrate may, if for reasons to be recorded by him he is satisfied that it is in the interests ofjustice to do so and if the case is one in which bail may lawfully be granted, release the person arrested on bail conditional on his appearing before the appropriate court in Malaysia at a time to be specified in the bond and bail bond.

In these Rules, "offence" means a seizable offence or an offence on conviction, with imprisonment for a term exceeding six tion months under the laws of Brunei Darussalam or Malaysia.
